components.css: .ds-line { background: var(--slate); color: var(--chalk-2); font-family: var(--f-body); font-size: 1.3rem; line-height: 1.6; padding: 1.5rem; margin: 0; } .ds-org { position: relative; display: inline-block; padding: 0 0.32em; margin: 0 0.04em; color: #fff; white-space: nowrap; isolation: isolate; text-decoration: none; text-shadow: 0 1px 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35); } .ds-org::before { content: ""; position: absolute; z-index: -1; inset: 0.08em -0.06em 0.02em; background: var(--hue); opacity: 0.62; transform: skewX(-6deg) rotate(-0.8deg); border-radius: 0.12em 0.4em 0.18em 0.5em; transition: opacity 0.4s var(--ease-out), transform 0.5s var(--ease-out); } .ds-org-2::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0.1em; right: 0.1em; bottom: -0.12em; height: 0.13em; background: var(--hue2); opacity: 0.9; transform: rotate(-0.8deg); border-radius: 1em; } .ds-org:hover::before { opacity: 0.85; transform: skewX(-6deg) rotate(-0.8deg) scale(1.04); } .ds-org:focus-visible { outline: 2px dashed var(--chalk); outline-offset: 4px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-tools { display: flex; gap: 0.25rem; padding: 1rem; background: var(--slate-lo); } .ds-tool { appearance: none; border: 0; background: none; cursor: pointer; font-family: var(--f-display); font-style: italic; font-size: 1rem; color: var(--chalk-2); display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.55rem; height: 2.75rem; padding: 0 0.6rem; border-radius: 0.4rem; transition: color 0.3s var(--ease-out); } .ds-tool:hover { color: var(--chalk); } .ds-tool:focus-visible { outline: 2px dashed var(--chalk); outline-offset: 4px; } .ds-piece { width: 2.6rem; height: auto; transform: translateY(3px); transition: transform 0.4s var(--ease-out); } .ds-tool:hover .ds-piece { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-tool[aria-pressed="true"] { color: var(--chalk); } .ds-tool[aria-pressed="true"] .ds-piece { transform: translateY(-5px) rotate(-14deg); } .ds-tool:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; } .ds-tool:disabled .ds-piece { transform: translateY(3px); }

narrative.overview:
The whole site is one deep slate board after a good CMU seminar: a derivation of a person, set in Computer Modern and rendered as chalk. Ink is a single warm chalk white in three strengths; the board carries grain, a faint ruled texture, and half-erased equations left from the previous lecture. Content reads like a paper written on a board: an abstract, a notation table, lemmas with boxed results, numbered references, and office hours.

Density is low and the board is mostly unprinted. Each section is a full-width panel separated by a hairline seam, with one display-serif heading that writes itself on from left to right. Ornament is never decorative: every mark is a piece of mathematical notation (an underbrace, a box around a result, a therefore sign, an arrow) drawn as a chalk stroke.

Colour exists only as code. Institution names sit on a rubbed smear of coloured chalk in their brand hue; nothing else on the board is coloured. The visitor can pick up chalk from the tray and draw on the board, then erase it. The world refuses the dark-mode developer portfolio: no hero-plus-skill-pills-plus-card-grid.
keyCharacteristics: One slate board, one chalk ink in three strengths, colour reserved for institution smears.
Computer Modern throughout: Serif for display and math, Concrete for reading, Typewriter for codes, dates and numbers.
Notation as ornament: underbraces, boxes, ∴ and → are drawn or typeset, never iconography.
Chalk texture comes from three SVG displacement filters, not from images.
Motion is a write-on: clip reveals for headings, stroke-draws for marks, once, and fully visible without JS or under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Colour Is Code Rule
rules.body: Colour appears only as an institution's smear behind its own name. No coloured headings, buttons, links, borders or highlights. The chalk and eraser drawings in the tray depict their real objects and are the only exception.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: All text and marks are chalk white at one of three strengths (chalk, chalk-2, chalk-3). Hierarchy comes from strength, size and italic, never from a second hue.

rules.name: The Typeset Not Styled Rule
rules.body: Every face is Computer Modern. Emphasis is italic or bold Serif as in a paper (Lemma heads in bold, lemma names in italic); never uppercase tracking, never a sans.

rules.name: The Typewriter Means Data Rule
rules.body: CMU Typewriter is used only for codes, dates, keys and numbers. It never sets prose or navigation.

rules.name: The Board Is Flat Rule
rules.body: Nothing written on the board casts a shadow. Only the tray and the hint, which are objects in front of it, are lifted.

dos: **Do** set every institution name in an institution smear with its brand hue from `orgs`, and add new institutions there rather than in CSS.
**Do** draw ornament as notation: a chalk box for a result, an underbrace for an annotation, ∴ before a conclusion, → between recipe and result.
**Do** run chalk texture through the shared #chalk, #chalk-soft and #chalk-line filters: heavy for the name, soft for headings and links, line for strokes.
**Do** separate content with 1px seams at 16% chalk and leave the board open; panels breathe at clamp(4.5rem, 9vw, 8rem).
**Do** keep reveals one-shot, ease-out expo, visible without JS, and removed under reduced motion.
**Do** reach for chalk-2 and italic before reaching for a smaller size.
donts: **Don't** colour anything except institution smears: no accent buttons, coloured links, coloured headings or tinted panels.
**Don't** use any face outside Computer Modern; route new symbols through the CM Symbols subset instead of letting a system font fill the glyph.
**Don't** build the dark-mode developer portfolio: no skill pills, no card grid, no boxed cards with fills or borders on all four sides.
**Don't** cast shadows from anything written on the board.
**Don't** use CMU Typewriter for prose, headings or navigation.
**Don't** put a label above a heading; context goes into an italic subtitle below it.
